target_state.assertion: audio service startup contains no late Binder thread-pool shrink operation
target_state.evidence: Current service configures its RPC pool before join and has no conflicting ABinderProcess_setThreadPoolMaxThreadCount call.

rules.rationale: A13 stopped calling ABinderProcess_setThreadPoolMaxThreadCount(1) after the vndbinder pool had already started, preventing the fatal 'threadpool cannot be shrunk' assertion. The Android 16 service no longer has that conflicting NDK Binder call and configures a single 16-thread RPC pool before joining it, preserving the crash fix through the current service architecture.
rules.necessity: Required semantically: the audio HAL service must not shrink a running Binder pool. No A13 line should be copied because the obsolete API sequence no longer exists.
rules.performance: The current 16-thread pool can consume more stack memory than the old one-thread request but supports concurrent HAL traffic and is the Android 16 service design.
rules.security: Avoids an unauthenticated service abort path. Binder concurrency still requires thread-safe HAL implementations.
validation_evidence: A13 crash trace and one-line workaround were compared with the final Android-16 service startup sequence; no late ABinderProcess thread-count mutation remains. Audio runtime regression is pending.

rules.rationale: Android 16 preserves the complete A13 FPS contract: read bst.max_fps, update the framebuffer vsync period, expose the new period through HWC2 display attributes and notify SurfaceFlinger through the refresh callback. Follow-up commits remove the unvalidated direct callback and restore it with null checks, mutex-protected state, atomic period publication, per-thread timing and callback invocation outside the lock.
rules.necessity: Required for host-configured frame-rate changes to affect framebuffer HWC timing and reach SurfaceFlinger.
rules.performance: One property read per second in the vsync thread. The callback runs only when the period changes; no per-frame property read is introduced. Very high/invalid FPS values are rejected when the computed period is non-positive.
rules.security: The privileged bst.max_fps property controls display scheduling. Parsing is bounded and callbacks are null-checked and invoked without holding the adapter mutex, reducing deadlock and crash risk.
validation_evidence: Final Android-16 source contains libcutils linkage, refresh registration, synchronized one-second polling, atomic refresh-period publication and lock-safe callback delivery. Component commits ea0df662, fc6ad600 and bf800caa encode the implementation and safety follow-ups; runtime FPS regression remains pending.
